subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should a failed operator-triggered cron run increment scheduler consecutive-error state and emit scheduler failure alerts, or should manual-run observability be recorded separately from scheduler retry and alert state?
rationale: The final branch intentionally changed manual failures to update counters and alerts, while the requested behavior and PR summary describe manual runs as non-mutating for scheduler-owned state. This is an operator-facing semantics choice rather than a mechanical implementation detail.

options.title: Keep manual failures scheduler-neutral
options.body: Preserve manual outcome visibility without contributing to scheduler counters, retry escalation, or scheduled failure alerts.

options.title: Count manual failures as scheduler failures
options.body: Retain the final-commit behavior and document that manual verification failures affect subsequent error history and alerts.

recommendation.title: Keep manual failures scheduler-neutral
recommendation.body: Preserve manual outcome visibility without contributing to scheduler counters, retry escalation, or scheduled failure alerts.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged cron work covers adjacent next-run and persisted scheduling invariants that this decision must preserve.
